the hybrid nature of somatic hybrids was confirmed by cytological, phenotypic and molecular methods, that tetraploid hybrids showed numerical and structural chromosome mutations, that most of the tetraploids were more vigorous than dihaploid parents, that most of tetraploid hybrids had a cpDN pattern identical to one parental line, that one tetraploid hybrid had a high percentage of viable pollen grains and that most of hexaploid hybrids had a high percentage pollen viability.

(1) the somatic hybrids are more vigorous than their parents; (2) the tetraploid hybrids are more uniform than aneu- ploid hybrids; (3) the chloroplast genome in somatic hybrids can be determined by RFLPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of somatic hybrids with a high level of ploidy.
the use of somatic hybridization for the generation of new potato cultivars and with the development of methods to characterize the resulting hybrids.
the production of somatic hybrids of potato, the cytological and phenotypic analysis of these hybrids and their use as a starting point for the production of new varieties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hybrid nature of somatic hybrids can be confirmed by cytological and molecular methods, but that the phenotypic expression of somatic hybrids is highly dependent on the parental genotypes and ploidy levels.
the tetraploid hybrids with a full chromosome number are more uniform than the aneuploid hybrids.
the tetraploid and some of the hexaploid somatics are superior to the parents and could be considered as potential breeding materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of dihaploids in fusion experiments is advantageous in the production of somatic hybrids with a full complement of chromosomes.
the tetraploid hybrids showed more vigour than dihaploids.
the somatic hybrid plants are more vigorous and uniform in morphology than the dihaploids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain somatic hybrids with a high degree of ploidy variation and a wide range of morphological characteristics.
the tetraploid hybrids have a high potential for breeding.
somatic hybrids are more vigorous than dihaploid parents, and can be grouped into different classes on the base of their phenotypic traits.
